title: Cabinet Refinishing in Archer, FL | Painted Kitchen Cabinets
description: Cabinet refinishing in Archer, FL: degrease, sand, bond-prime, and spray waterborne urethane enamel on oak, maple, and painted farmhouse kitchen cabinets.
heroIntro: A new kitchen color without tearing out sound cabinet boxes. We prep, prime, and apply a hard waterborne urethane enamel built for a working farmhouse kitchen.

questions: Can oak cabinets be painted without the grain showing through?
How long does cabinet refinishing take in Archer?
Is it better to paint or replace kitchen cabinets?

sections.h2: Why Archer kitchens are good candidates
body: Many kitchens in Archer's farmhouses and ranch homes have solid cabinet boxes that were built to last, wrapped in an orange-toned oak or a dated stain. Ripping them out is expensive and loud. Cabinet refinishing in Archer, FL keeps the boxes and doors you already have and gives them a durable painted finish in a color that fits the rest of the house.

Farmhouse kitchens also work hard. Canning, big family meals, and the back door opening straight into the kitchen all mean grease, steam, and handling. The finish has to be harder than wall paint, which is why we use waterborne urethane enamel on every cabinet job.

Hardware is part of the decision, too. Many owners swap dated pulls for something that suits the new color, and filling or re-drilling holes is easiest while the doors are already off. Tell us at the walkthrough so it lands on the estimate instead of becoming a surprise.

bullets: Remove doors, drawer fronts, and hardware; label every piece for return to its spot
Degrease thoroughly, since cooking film is the most common cause of peeling
Scuff-sand to dull the old finish and fill open grain where requested
Apply a bonding primer suited to oak, maple, or previously painted surfaces
Spray two coats of waterborne urethane enamel for a smooth, cleanable surface
Reinstall, adjust, and walk the finished kitchen with you
body: Boxes and face frames are masked and sprayed in place, with counters, floors, and appliances covered. Want an exact match to a door from another room or a leftover can? We can match it and show full-size drawdowns before committing.

sections.h2: Oak grain: hide it or let it show
body: Painted oak will show its grain texture unless the open pores are filled before priming. Some owners like that texture for a farmhouse look; others want a smooth, modern surface. We will show you both on a sample door. Our article on painting oak cabinets walks through the trade-offs, and refinish vs. replace helps you decide whether your boxes are worth keeping.

sections.h2: Timing and living around the work
body: Most kitchen cabinet painting projects take several working days from removal to reinstall, because enamel needs time between coats to level and harden. You can still use the house; we keep the work area contained. Many Archer owners pair cabinets with fresh walls through interior painting in Archer so the kitchen is finished at once. See our full cabinet painting and refinishing service for more detail.

faqs.q: Will painted cabinets peel in a busy kitchen?
faqs.a: Peeling usually comes from skipped degreasing or no bonding primer. We do both, then apply waterborne urethane enamel, which cures much harder than wall paint.

faqs.q: Can you paint thermofoil or laminate cabinets?
faqs.a: Some can be coated with the right bonding primer if the surface is still firmly attached. The crew lead checks condition at the walkthrough.

faqs.q: Can I choose a color to match my farmhouse trim?
faqs.a: Yes. We match from a chip, a door, or a leftover can and show you a full-size drawdown before spraying.
